cards.text: Job just said, "I know that my Redeemer lives" (Job 19:25), and he warned his friends that they should fear the sword themselves (Job 19:29). Now Zophar the Naamathite, one of the three friends who came to comfort Job (Job 2:11), replies. And friend, he is NOT easing into it.
Zophar opens by saying there's turmoil within him and he HAS to answer. You know when a message comes in and you're typing back before you even finish reading it? That's this man right here.

cards.question: Zophar says something inside him compels him to answer Job. What is it?
Job just warned his friends. True or false: Zophar says he has heard a rebuke that insults him.

cards.text: Then Zophar asks Job, Do you not know? He's about to bring up something he says has been true for a long, LONG time.

cards.question: Zophar says this truth about the wicked is old. How far back does he say it goes?

answers.text: Since man was placed on the earth

cards.question: Zophar's whole speech is aimed at the wicked. He says that all that time, the triumph of the wicked has been ___.

cards.text: Then Zophar says, though the wicked man's arrogance reaches the heavens and his head touches the clouds... Friend, I stretch ALL the way up on my gold base and my head touches the second oven rack.

cards.question: Zophar says that even with his head up in the clouds, the wicked man will ___ forever.

cards.text: And Zophar picks a picture you will NOT forget. The wicked man will perish forever, "like his own dung." Zophar doesn't soften it one bit.

cards.question: True or false: Zophar says the people who once saw the wicked man will ask, ‘Where is he?’

cards.text: Zophar says he'll fly away like a dream, chased away like a vision in the night. Like the dream you SWEAR you'll remember, and by the second snooze it's GONE.

cards.question: True or false: Zophar says the eye that saw the wicked man will see him again someday.

cards.text: Zophar says even the wicked man's place won't behold him anymore. Oh, I know that one. One day a shiny new stamper is sitting in MY spot on the counter, and I'm in the back of the junk drawer.

cards.question: Zophar says the wicked man's own hands must give his wealth back. So what does he say the man's sons will do?

answers.text: Seek the favor of the poor

cards.question: Zophar talks about the youthful vigor that fills the wicked man's bones. Where does he say it ends up?

answers.text: Lying with him in the dust
Keeping him strong into old age

cards.text: Now Zophar switches to a picture of eating. Evil is sweet in the wicked man's mouth, and he hides it under his tongue and can't bear to let it go, like the last bite of cookie you keep in your cheek so nobody asks you to share.

cards.question: Zophar says evil tastes sweet to the wicked man at first. What happens once it reaches his stomach?
The wicked man's hands already had to give back his riches. Zophar says he swallows ___ but vomits it out, and God will force it from his stomach.

cards.text: And Zophar is NOT done with the snakes. He says the wicked man will suck the poison of cobras, and the fangs of a viper will kill him.

cards.question: True or false: Zophar says the wicked man will enjoy the rivers flowing with honey and cream.

cards.text: Zophar says he must return the fruit of his labor without consuming it, and he can't enjoy the profits of his trading. Like payday hitting and the bills taking it ALL before you even see it.

cards.question: Now Zophar says why the wicked man loses everything he worked for. What reason does he give?

answers.text: He oppressed and forsook the poor
He never worked a single day
He gave his wealth to strangers

cards.question: True or false: Zophar says the wicked man seized houses he did not build.
Zophar keeps coming back to food and swallowing. What does he say about the wicked man's appetite?

cards.text: Because of that appetite, Zophar says, he can't escape with his treasure. Nothing is left for him to consume, so his prosperity won't last.

cards.question: True or false: Zophar says the wicked man will be at peace as long as he has plenty.
Zophar's picture is all about eating. True or false: he says God's fury rains down on the wicked man while he eats.
Zophar says the wicked man flees from an iron weapon. Can he outrun what's coming?

cards.text: Zophar says the arrow is drawn out of his back, the gleaming point from his liver. And terrors come over him.

cards.question: Zophar says total darkness is reserved for the wicked man's treasures, and a ___ nobody fanned will consume him and what's left in his tent.
The wicked man hid evil under his tongue. But Zophar says the heavens will ___ his iniquity.

cards.text: The earth rises up against him too. And Zophar says the possessions of his house will be removed, flowing away on the day of God's wrath.

cards.question: Zophar wraps up his whole speech in one line. What does he call everything he just described?

answers.text: The wicked man's portion from God

cards.text: That's Zophar's whole speech, friend. And trust me, this conversation is FAR from over.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 10 quotes "like his own dung.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The question asks 'Where does he say it ends up?' The right answer 'Lying with him in the dust' and the wrong answer 'Passed on to his sons' both answer where. 'Keeping him strong into old age' doesn't name a place, so it isn't the same kind of answer as the other two.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The question says evil 'tastes sweet to the wicked man at first.' The words 'at first' rule out the wrong answer 'It stays sweet for good' before the baker picks.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The right answer 'It sours into cobra venom' says that 'it' (the evil) sours. Job 20:14 says 'his food sours into the venom of cobras.' The card should call the thing what the text calls it, his food.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The setup says the wicked man 'had to give back his riches,' and the blank is 'wealth.' Riches means wealth, so the setup gives the answer away and rules out 'bread' and 'wine.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card says the wicked man's hands 'already had to give back his riches.' Job 20:10 says 'his own hands must return his wealth.' Nothing in the text says this has already happened, and 'already' adds a time order the text doesn't give.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: Card 6 just told the baker that Zophar speaks of the 'fruit of his labor' and the 'profits of his trading.' That rules out the wrong answer 'He never worked a single day' before the baker picks.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card only restates Job 20:20-21. There's no reaction, comparison or storyteller line, so Papa Dorin's voice is missing.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The card says 'Zophar's picture is all about eating.' That isn't true of the speech, which also uses dreams, arrows, fire, darkness, the heavens and the earth. The claim also points the baker straight to the 'True' answer about God's fury raining down while he eats.

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: This story card only restates Job 20:25. There's no reaction or storyteller line, so Papa Dorin's voice is missing.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The question says 'a ___ nobody fanned.' Only fire gets fanned, so the setup rules out 'flood' and 'storm.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The setup says 'The wicked man hid evil under his tongue. But…' and treats the heavens exposing his iniquity (Job 20:27) as the answer to that hiding (Job 20:12). The text never links these two verses, and Job 20:12 is part of the image of savoring food, not of hiding sin from view.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This story card only restates Job 20:27-28. There's no reaction or storyteller line, so Papa Dorin's voice is missing.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The last story card contains only the 'story isn't over' line and tells no verse, but it cites Job 20:29. The rule says a story card cites the verses it tells, and this card tells none.
findings.question: What should a closing story card cite when it carries only the 'story isn't over' line and tells no verse: the last verse of the passage, the whole passage, or something else?
